clue.text: Compact I fail to break — it's done and can't be altered

definitions.text: it's done and can't be altered

indicators.note: to break the words is to smash them apart and reassemble their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to smash a powder compact shrugs it off as a done deal that cannot be undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' signals rearranging the letters of COMPACT I FAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a thing already accomplished and presented as settled, beyond any reversal.

clue.text: Money is put together by saint

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and is still that of Switzerland
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holy man assembles a sum of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put together by' just joins the two pieces before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: St Francis of Assisi is a famous saint, founder of the Franciscan friars.

clue.text: Relative pronoun initially, now largely archaic -whoso

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the relative pronoun 'whoso' has largely fallen out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative pronoun' reads as one grammatical term, but 'Relative' is the definition and 'pronoun' gives I; 'initially' then takes the first letters of 'now largely archaic whoso'.
explanation.definitionFit: A family member by marriage, such as a spouse's mother, is a relative.

clue.text: What Petruchio wanted to do, they say — wrangle

indicators.note: they say tells us the phrase is spoken and the answer is what we hear

parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, Petruchio sets out to change (alter) the shrewish Kate

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare question: what was Petruchio's aim, and was it simply to argue?
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to argue heatedly, which is what a wrangle is.

clue.text: Where, say, to make a change in the team

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the place-name and hear the answer

parts.note: the 'where' is a place to make a change: Crewe, an English town famous as a railway junction where passengers change trains

explanation.surface: A coach asks where to make a substitution in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where ... to make a change' describes CREWE, the Cheshire railway junction town where travellers change trains; said aloud it gives the word for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a team working together, as on a ship or in rowing.

clue.text: Christian, perhaps, is silent, holding in an expression of hesitation

indicators.note: holding means the word for silent wraps around the next piece

parts.note: silent means mute
taken as written
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A man named Christian is quiet, keeping an 'um' or 'er' to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the container. Fletcher Christian led the 1789 mutiny on HMS Bounty, so 'Christian, perhaps' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian led the 1789 revolt on the Bounty, making him the most famous rebel sailor.

clue.text: Dance round after mischievous child

indicators.note: after puts the ring-shaped letter behind the word for the naughty child

parts.note: a limb (short for 'limb of Satan') is an old word for a little imp
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dance performed around a naughty youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMB, short for 'limb of Satan', is an old British term for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which the dancer leans back to pass under a low bar.

clue.text: Study to improve a language at university

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
up is used of someone in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone studies a foreign language at college to get better at it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university while in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush up a skill is to work at it and refine it until it is better.

clue.text: Governor takes control in this

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor
a rein is a means of control

explanation.surface: A ruler seizes power in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: HE (His Excellency) is how a governor is addressed; 'takes' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word meaning within this document or place, as in 'the terms stated herein'.

clue.text: Tell man to change portion

indicators.note: to change the words is to rearrange their letters into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to tell a man to alter his share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' signals rearranging the letters of TELL MAN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a share allocated to someone, as a portion is.

clue.text: By the sound of it, a sweet creature

indicators.note: by the sound of it says we hear the word for the dessert spoken

parts.note: a mousse is a light, airy dessert, a sweet in British usage

explanation.surface: Something described as a sweet little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' is a British word for a dessert course; MOUSSE said aloud gives the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large North American deer, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Playwright was mostly kept in line

indicators.note: kept in means the shortened word is placed inside the word for a line

parts.note: a cord is a line or string

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word was

explanation.surface: A dramatist was largely made to toe the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' and 'kept in' are the two indicators; 'line' is a cord or string, not a row. Noel Coward was an English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward wrote Private Lives and Blithe Spirit, which makes him a noted dramatist.

clue.text: Trouble I mention very quickly

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker raises a problem promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' signals rearranging the letters of I MENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for instantly, with barely any time passing.

clue.text: The way papers float in the wind

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: How sheets of paper drift about on a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way papers' reads as describing loose paper; ST (street) plus REAM build the verb used of a flag flying out.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner or hair that flows out on the breeze is said to stream.

clue.text: Adapt oneself again to study, right?

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
just means right or fair

explanation.surface: A question whether one must get used to study once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to settle back in after a change, adapting to circumstances anew.

clue.text: Stretch one learning English at that time

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British L-plates
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A student of English was making an effort back then.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to make it longer, as stretching does.

clue.text: George satisfied Richard, we hear, using simple figures

parts.note: Geo is an abbreviation of the name George
to meet a demand is to satisfy it

indicators.note: we hear says the pet name is heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: Rick is a short form of Richard

explanation.surface: Reportedly George pleased Richard by drawing basic shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns RICK into RIC by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometric patterns are built from basic shapes such as lines, circles and triangles.

clue.text: Obtain an adjournment — judge overcome

parts.note: to count something as is to judge or deem it so
out means unconscious, overcome as a boxer is

explanation.surface: A lawyer wins a delay after the judge is overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons a sitting was 'counted out' and adjourned when too few members were present.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting out a parliamentary sitting for lack of a quorum forced it to adjourn.

clue.text: Companion takes tea with the president

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
Juan Peron was President of Argentina

explanation.surface: A friend has a cup of tea with the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies a young woman for propriety, acting as her escort.

clue.text: Players the French keep

parts.note: the cast of a play are its players
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Actors from France hold on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' reads as a verb but is the noun: the strongest tower of a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the central tower of a medieval fortress, and by extension the fortress itself.

clue.text: Gun dogs

explanation.definitionFit: A pom-pom is a quick-firing anti-aircraft cannon; poms are Pomeranians, a small toy breed, so two of them.

clue.text: Sort of man found in centre of boat

explanation.definitionFit: A midshipman is a junior naval officer, so this word qualifies 'man'; it also names the middle part of a vessel.

clue.text: Stays a day abroad surrounded by children

indicators.note: surrounded by means the foreign word for a day sits inside the word for children

parts.note: sons are male children
jour is French for day

explanation.surface: A family's offspring go with someone on a day trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' signals the container, and 'abroad' tells you the day is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary visit, so 'sojourns' means stays for a while.

clue.text: Not qualified to speak

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or absolute, with no qualification; as a verb it means to say aloud.

clue.text: Back in a moment

explanation.definitionFit: To support a motion is to back it; a short instant is a moment, as in 'wait a sec'.

clue.text: Beach has some aroma hard to identify

indicators.note: some means only part of the words aroma hard is taken

explanation.surface: A stretch of shore gives off a whiff that is hard to place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'to identify' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha was a code name for one of the D-Day landing beaches in Normandy.

clue.text: River responsible for erosion

explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a river in north-east England flowing through Durham; wear is also gradual damage from use.

clue.text: Composer a heel, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the word for the tilt is heard rather than read

parts.note: a list is a heel or lean of a ship to one side

explanation.surface: A musician is called a cad, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' suggests a cad, but here it is a ship's tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian pianist and composer of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Gull above the water

parts.note: over means above
a reach is a stretch of river water between bends or locks

explanation.surface: A seabird hovers over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' looks like a bird but is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull is to trick or dupe, and to overreach someone is to outwit them by cunning.

clue.text: Malady upsetting crew mars trip

indicators.note: upsetting means the words are knocked over and their letters reordered

explanation.surface: An illness spoils the sailors' journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' signals rearranging the letters of CREW MARS TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp of the hand muscles from long spells of handwriting is a recognised ailment.
